name: libnetfilter-queue
desc: Userspace API to packets queued by the kernel packet filter
why: A userspace door into packets held by the kernel firewall, letting you intercept and rewrite traffic in real time.

brief.what_it_is: libnetfilter_queue is a userspace C library that gives programs an API to packets the Linux kernel packet filter has queued for them. A program receives queued packets from the kernel's nfnetlink_queue subsystem, inspects them, and sends back a verdict or reinjects an altered packet. The homepage describes it as a library, not a standalone tool, so its inputs are kernel-queued packets and its outputs are verdicts and modified packets.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage says it is part of a system that deprecates the old ip_queue / libipq mechanism. It was previously known as libnfnetlink_queue.
brief.how_it_works: The kernel's nfnetlink_queue subsystem holds packets that firewall rules send to a queue, and the library passes them to userspace over netlink. The program then issues a verdict on each packet or reinjects a changed version back into the kernel. The homepage names the two main features as receiving queued packets and issuing verdicts and/or reinjecting altered packets, but does not go into further detail.
brief.install_notes: The homepage says libnetfilter_queue requires libnfnetlink and a kernel that includes the nfnetlink_queue subsystem, meaning Linux 2.6.14 or later. No install steps, build commands, or first-run configuration appear on the homepage. Documentation is linked as doxygen-generated API docs, which I did not fetch.
brief.standout: It is the userspace end of the netfilter queue, so a program can rewrite live traffic in the kernel's firewall path rather than only observing it. The project positions it as the modern replacement for the older ip_queue / libipq interface.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage carries a 1999-2025 copyright and a netfilter news list, but the news items I saw are for other projects (nftables, libnftnl, iptables, conntrack-tools), not libnetfilter_queue, and I could not find a release date for this library. The git tree at git.netfilter.org, which would show the last commit, was blocked by an Anubis proof-of-work challenge and I could not read it.
brief.caveats: Linux-only, since it depends on the kernel's nfnetlink_queue subsystem. Requires libnfnetlink and a kernel with nfnetlink_queue. The homepage does not mention a license in the text I read, though the site has a Licensing section, which I did not open. The homepage does not show examples or usage. The git tree was unreachable from this fetch, so I could not confirm recent activity.
